title: Clinical effectiveness of a new collagen matrix in a randomised comparison with the addition of either platelet-rich fibrin or alternatively hyaluronic acid in intrabony defects - pilot study
summary:
The research project investigates the clinical success of a surgical complementary therapy for periodontitis. A minor dental surgical procedure is performed under local anaesthesia using a volume-stable, three-dimensionally cross-linked collagen membrane ("FibroGide", Geistlich Biomaterials, Wolhusen, Switzerland). Collagen is a structural protein that is usually found in connective tissue. A membrane is formed from it, i.e. a kind of thin membrane with a demarcating function. In the study, this collagen membrane is combined with either thrombocyte-rich fibrin (cell-rich fluid produced from your blood) or with hyaluronic acid (a connective tissue component, Hyadent, Regedent). Allocation to the respective test group is randomised, i.e. randomly, as with the tossing of a coin, in order to obtain results that are as uninfluenced as possible; the probability of being allocated to a test group is 50%. The aim is to find out whether these two product combination options could show clinically comparable results with less co-morbidity (concomitant disease). 
To conduct the study, we need participants who have already completed initial periodontitis therapy and still have teeth that require treatment. These teeth must require regenerative periodontitis therapy. This means that there must be a vertical bone defect and a probing depth of ≥ 6mm. Regenerative means the restoration of the previous healthy state, that is the regeneration of new tissue.

interventions.name:
During periodontal surgery on the study tooth, one test group receives the collagen matrix in combination with platelet-rich fibrin (PRF for short), which is obtained from the test subjects' own blood.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minimum age of 18 years
Completed anti-infective, non-surgical periodontitis therapy (completed at least 3 months ago)
Generally healthy state of health
At least one tooth with a vertical bone defect and residual probing depth of ≥ 6 mm 
Presence of adequate oral hygiene after determination of the FMPI "Full mouth plaque index"
Periodontal regenerative measures should be desired
Willingness to participate in the study and the necessary follow-up examinations
Exclusion criteria:
17 years or younger
Pregnant patients or those planning a pregnancy
Existing contraindication for oral surgery
Presence of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus or other uncontrolled systemic disease
Taking medication with a high dose of steroids
Existing bone disease
Patients with radiotherapy or immunosuppression
Existing infection or vascular compromise at the surgical site
Treatment with antibiotics or anti-inflammatory medication (>3 times/week) in the last 3 months
Presence of oral lesions (ulcerations, malignant changes, lichen planus)
Existing / previously existing malignant diseases of the oral cavity 
Inadequate oral hygiene
Smoking > 10 cigarettes per day
